## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/8871-page-node-refuses-breadcrumbs.md`

- names `layout/src/NavigationRenderer.tsx` → `packages/layout/src/NavigationRenderer.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **What was measured, on this branch's base `93127bd6f`.** Zero readers, with a **point-access** probe rather than a bare word: on that base `\.breadcrumbs` scores 0 tree-wide (exit 1) against `\.breadcrumb\b`'s **12** files tree-wide (**10** under `packages/`) as the lit control. At head the same two probes read 16 and 13 and `\.breadcrumbs` is exit 0 over 4 files — every hit one of this branch's own four files (this changeset, the refusal pin, `layout.ts`, `zod/layout.zod.ts`) quoting the probe string, and the pin's own exclusions put head back at exit 1. The base reading is the measurement; the head reading is this branch's echo of it. The bare word would have lied — it also names Sentry's own unrelated concept (`app-shell/src/observability/sentry.ts`) and appears in two comments listing UI surfaces (`core/src/utils/record-title.ts`, `layout/src/NavigationRenderer.tsx`), so a bare probe reports five readers that do not exist.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `6cc910b6d` (merge-base with origin/main): 2 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1246 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (1811 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/35527641826)

## ACCEPT — PR #10160, card objectui#10119. ⚠️ The card's PREMISE was falsified, and that is the headline of this acceptance.

Reviewed by the `domain:ui` execution seat (Seat: domain:ui#2, session `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`) at 2026-09-20T18:25Z. `Implemented-by:` an `os-dev` subagent of this session · `Reviewed-by:` this seat.

### ⭐ `premise_still_valid: false` — and this seat checked rather than took it

The card says an app nav item's `visible` CEL 「is not evaluated by the Console shell」. **On today's `main` it is.** Read by this seat in `NavigationRenderer.tsx`: the item renderer carries `if (!evalVis(item.visible)) return null;`, and the area-derivation walk carries `if (!evaluateVisibility(item.visible)) continue;`.

The dev reached the same answer from the other side, and its version is the stronger one: under ablation — the fix reverted on disk, the mutation proved by the guard-marker count going 4 → 0 — the run reads **2 failed | 5 passed**, and ⭐ **the 5 that stay green are the card's headline.** A pin set that passes without the fix is telling you the fix was not for that.

The card was filed against a Console build served next to `@objectstack/*` 17.2.0; the gating landed in `app-shell`/`layout` 17.1.0, which versions on its own cadence. ⇒ a true report about the build in front of the reporter, ⛔ not a true statement about this repository. Recorded on the card itself so the archive does not mislead a later reader.

### ⭐ But the card's REPRO pointed at the real thing, and the fix is not cosmetic

The repro deliberately carried a predicate on **both a group and its leaf** — and the nesting rule is exactly what was broken. Two live defects:

1. **A pinned descendant escaped its hidden ancestor.** Re-derived by this seat from `collectPinnedItems`' body on `origin/main`: it recurses through `item.children` pushing any `pinned` node, ⛔ without ever asking whether the node it descended through survived its own guards. ⇒ a pinned item under a group gated away by `visible` kept rendering in Favorites **for the very user the predicate excludes** — and `requiredPermissions`, `requiresObject` and `requiresService` leaked by the same route. ⚠️ This is the gate actually leaking, and it is arguably worse than what the card reported.
2. **An empty group rendered a husk** — a labelled disclosure onto nothing once every child was hidden, making `hasVisibleNavigationItems`' documented 「can never disagree with the rendered navigation」 invariant false.

### The dispatch's three demands, all met

- **Reuse, ⛔ do not re-implement.** `evaluateVisibility` (the shipped `ExpressionProvider` evaluator that routes CEL envelopes to `@objectstack/formula` — the same one the action capability gates and the record-form field gates use), plus `buildExpressionUser` and `hasVisibleNavigationItems`, which fix (b) **calls** rather than re-asks. ⭐ The only new symbol, `passesNavItemGuards`, is a **de-duplication**: the per-item guard sequence existed twice and was missing once, in `collectPinnedItems` — which is how both defects arose. Three cards this shift with the same root shape, and this one removes the duplication instead of adding a third copy.
- **The nesting rule, settled and stated.** A group whose own predicate is false takes its entire subtree on every path the shell surfaces it, Favorites included; a group whose children are all hidden is absent too. One statement decides both, so the sidebar and the area switcher cannot disagree.
- **The failure direction, chosen and pinned.** **FAIL-OPEN** for an unevaluable predicate, which is this tier's already-ruled policy. The reasoning is right and this seat endorses it: hiding a nav entry is **presentation**; the server still enforces object and record permissions on every route the entry leads to, so 「show on error」 leaks an *entry the server still refuses*, while 「hide on error」 would silently delete a user's navigation with no diagnostic. ⛔ No server-side check was touched, and ⛔ the change is correctly not described as a security fix.

### Clause-② — `no`, and ⚠️ this one needed a different check from the last two

`@object-ui/layout`'s barrel re-exports the changed module with `export * from './NavigationRenderer'` — so ⚠️ **any symbol exported there reaches the public face**, unlike the named-import barrels on PRs #10154 and #10158 where a new export stayed internal by construction. Here it is internal by choice: `passesNavItemGuards` is declared with ⛔ no `export`, and the whole diff adds zero `export` lines in that module. `--pair 10160` exits **0** via the `Clause-②-correction:` carrier; `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr objectstack-ai/objectui#10160` exits **0**.

### The one local red, and why it is ⛔ not this PR's

The dev's local full-suite run showed one `app-shell` failure. ⭐ It established non-attribution by measurement, ⛔ not by calling it a flake: base green on the same suite under the same load; the branch failing **twice, in a different file each time**, with the identical guard and the identical three URLs; and both named files passing in isolation on base and branch. **A defect a source change causes does not move between files between runs.**

⛔ And none of that was needed to land this: **CI reads 43 checks, 0 pending, 0 failed** on the head. The local phenomenon is filed as **objectui#10162** — a rotating innocent red under full-suite load, with the guard's own prescribed remedy — clearly marked as relayed, since this seat measured none of it.

⚠️ The PR body records that red as `NOT MEASURED`, because readings (1) and (2) arrived after the body was written. That is **dated, ⛔ not false**, so it stands as the push-time record; this acceptance and objectui#10162 carry the finished reading. (The distinction matters on this repo because a squash lands the body verbatim in `main`'s commit log.)

⛔ Not filed, agreed: `NavigationItem.visible` is declared `boolean | string` while the transport hands the gate a `{ dialect, source }` envelope. The declaration's own docblock says so and a spec-derived-unions pin holds it ⇒ a recorded boundary, not a finding. Carrier: any future change to that declaration.

43 checks, **0 pending, 0 failed**. Flipping ready and arming now.
